report.tagline: The app and website of the UK's best-known clothing and food retailer, with Sparks loyalty rewards built in.
report.simpleSummary: Marks & Spencer, or M&S, is a famous British chain that sells clothes, home goods and premium food. Its app lets you buy clothes online, reserve items, scan your Sparks loyalty card and get personal offers. In April 2025 hackers broke into its systems and M&S had to stop online orders for about seven weeks. It is now a well-known case of how a business handles a crisis.

overview.whatItDoes: M&S sells clothing, beauty, home and premium food in about 1,000 UK stores and online. The app handles clothing and home orders, Sparks loyalty, and store tools like click and collect. Food delivery is done by Ocado, where M&S owns half of Ocado Retail.
howItWorks: Shoppers browse and buy clothing, beauty and home items in the app; orders are delivered or collected in store.
Sparks is built into the app: shoppers scan it at the till and get personal offers, birthday treats and charity donations.
In-store, the app can check stock and scan to buy, and staff can order missing sizes for home delivery.
M&S Food online grocery is sold through Ocado.com, not the M&S app.
After the 2025 attack, M&S rebuilt systems with tighter identity checks and moved faster on a planned technology upgrade.
overview.valueProposition: Trusted quality clothing and food from a brand people know, with rewards for loyal shoppers and the choice to buy online or in store.

businessModel.summary: M&S makes money by selling its own-brand clothing, home goods and food at mid-to-premium prices. Online sales are mainly clothing and home. Sparks is not a revenue stream on its own but drives repeat visits and targeted offers.

revenueStreams.detail: Premium food in stores and via Ocado, the largest share of sales.
Own-brand clothing and home goods, in store and online.
M&S owns 50% of Ocado Retail, which sells M&S food online.

businessModel.pricing: Clothing is mid-priced, for example T-shirts around £10 to £15 and jumpers £25 to £60. Standard UK delivery around £4.99, with free click and collect on most orders. Sparks is free.
costDrivers: Technology, including rebuilding systems after the attack
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £60 online clothing order, M&S keeps about £33 in gross margin (clothing margins are around 55%). Picking, packing and delivery cost about £6 to £8, or less if collected in store. Marketing and payment add a few pounds. The 2025 attack showed how fragile this is: about £300 million of operating profit was lost when online orders stopped for 46 days.

howTheyGetUsers: Store traffic: about 1,000 UK stores send shoppers to the app
Social media hits like popular jeans and dresses
whatBringsUsersBack: Reliable basics like underwear and school uniform
Click and collect bringing people into stores
growth.moat: M&S has a trusted British brand built over 140 years, stores near most people, and a premium food business that brings shoppers back weekly. That trust is hard to copy, but the cyber attack showed it can be damaged quickly.

improvementIdeas.idea: An 'offline mode' fallback: let stores take online-style orders for home delivery even when the website is down.
improvementIdeas.problem: During the 2025 attack, online sales stopped completely.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Keep some online revenue during future outages.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Revenue lost per day of outage

improvementIdeas.idea: Passkeys and two-step login for all M&S accounts.
improvementIdeas.problem: Account security and trust after the data breach.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer account takeovers and more trust.

improvementIdeas.idea: In-app status page with clear updates during incidents.
improvementIdeas.problem: Customers were confused about what worked and what did not.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer support contacts and less frustration.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Support contacts per day during incidents

improvementIdeas.idea: Sparks offers that reward buying clothing after a food shop.
improvementIdeas.problem: Clothing online recovered slower than food.

pmLessons: Security is a product feature. One attack cost M&S about £300 million and weeks of online sales.
Plan for failure. A good product needs a backup plan for when systems go down.
Clear communication during a crisis protects trust as much as the fix itself.
Loyalty programmes like Sparks give data to personalise offers instead of cutting prices for everyone.

interviewQuestions.question: You are PM at M&S on day one of the cyber attack. What do you do first?
interviewQuestions.hint: Prioritise customer safety and communication, then keep stores running, then restore online in stages. Define what success looks like each week.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you rebuild customer trust after the data breach?
interviewQuestions.hint: Transparency, security features, rewards for staying. Measure trust via surveys and login rates.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase app usage among older shoppers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand barriers: tech confidence, value. Ideas: simpler login, Sparks-first home screen. Measure monthly active users.

interviewQuestions.question: What metrics would you track for the M&S app?
interviewQuestions.hint: Active users, conversion, Sparks scans, order reliability. Guardrails: uptime and security incidents.

interviewQuestions.question: Should M&S sell food in its own app instead of through Ocado?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh control and data against cost and Ocado's delivery strength. Suggest a test in one city.
